articles.body:
Estação Rei Pelé com ambientação especial para jogo da NFL no Rio — Foto: Divulgação

Para receber o público do NFL Rio Game 2026 , que acontece neste domingo (27), no Maracanã, a concessionária que administra o Metrô do Rio preparou uma operação especial e uma série de ações para orientar e aproximar os passageiros do evento. Uma delas é uma decoração especial na Estação Rei Pelé, a mais próxima do estádio.

Neste fim de semana, quem passar pelas estações das linhas 1, 2 e 4 será surpreendido pela voz do jornalista e comentarista Antony Curti, referência na cobertura da NFL no Brasil. Em uma ação especial, o comentarista gravou mensagens em português e inglês que serão reproduzidas nos avisos sonoros do sistema, com informações para facilitar o deslocamento dos torcedores até o Maracanã.

As mensagens orientam sobre as estações mais indicadas para acesso aos diferentes portões do estádio e reforçam a recomendação de utilizar o pagamento por aproximação diretamente nas catracas, agilizando tanto o embarque quanto o retorno após a partida.

Já a estação Rei Pelé/Maracanã recebeu uma ambientação especial para a partida. O espaço foi adesivado com elementos que remetem ao futebol americano, como linhas de jardas, marcações do campo, capacetes e a tradicional bola oval.

A intervenção transforma a estação em um dos pontos de chegada do público em uma experiência temática para os torcedores que vão acompanhar o duelo entre Baltimore Ravens e Dallas Cowboys.

Operação especial para o NFL Rio Game 2026

Metrõ preparou operação especial para jogo da NFL — Foto: Divulgação

Para atender ao público do evento, o MetrôRio terá uma operação especial neste domingo (27). O sistema funcionará das 7h às 23h, com reforço na oferta de trens durante os períodos de chegada e dispersão dos torcedores.

Também haverá reforço no efetivo de segurança e de operadores de estação, além de estruturas de controle de fluxo nas estações próximas ao Maracanã.

As linhas 1 e 4 operarão no trecho entre Uruguai e Jardim Oceânico/Barra da Tijuca, enquanto a Linha 2 funcionará entre Pavuna e General Osório/Ipanema. A transferência entre as linhas 1 e 2 poderá ser realizada no trecho entre as estações Central do Brasil e General Osório.

Para facilitar o deslocamento dos torcedores, o MetrôRio recomenda o uso do pagamento por aproximação (NFC) diretamente nas catracas. A alternativa permite que o passageiro embarque sem a necessidade de adquirir um bilhete antecipadamente.

Outra opção é comprar ou recarregar com antecedência os cartões de transporte Giro, Jaé e Riocard.

A tarifa do MetrôRio é de R$ 7,90 por viagem, tanto na ida quanto na volta.

articles.title: "Supportive wife vs. Black Widow": Hailee Steinfeld and Madison Beer face bizarre comparison as Justin Herbert's struggles continue
articles.summary: A viral social-media post has unexpectedly pulled Josh Allen and Hailee Steinfeld into the growing conversation surrounding Justin Herbert and Madison
articles.body: A viral social-media post has unexpectedly pulled Josh Allen and Hailee Steinfeld into the growing conversation surrounding Justin Herbert and Madison Beer. The post, shared by an X user, featured side-by-side images of the two NFL couples - Allen and Steinfeld on one side and Herbert and Beer on the other. The post essentially uses Allen and Steinfeld as the example of a supposedly supportive NFL relationship while placing Herbert and Beer on the other side of the comparison.Viral post pits Hailee Steinfeld against Madison Beer as Justin Herbert’s struggles spark debate“The supportive wife vs. The Black Widow archetype who sucks the life blood out of her man. Important to know the difference.”The post reflects a social-media narrative that has emerged after the Chargers opened the 2026 season 0-2. Beer has increasingly been dragged into conversations about Herbert's football performances despite there being no evidence that their relationship is affecting his play.Allen and Steinfeld provide an interesting contrast because their relationship has also received enormous attention from NFL and entertainment fans. The couple married in May 2025 and later welcomed their first child in 2026. Allen has also spoken publicly about how important Steinfeld is to him, saying she makes things easier for him and that marrying her was the most important decision he would make.That history is now being used by social-media users to construct a comparison between the two NFL relationships. But the viral post is an opinionated social-media framing, not an established assessment of either relationship.Madison Beer has been blamed for Herbert's rough startThe timing of the post comes after Herbert and the Chargers fell to 0-2. Beer attended both of Los Angeles' first two home games, and her presence became a talking point after the Chargers lost both games 26-14. A separate viral claim even falsely suggested that head coach Jim Harbaugh had banned Beer from Chargers games; that claim came from a satire account, and there is no credible evidence that Harbaugh has done so. The criticism has nevertheless continued.Former Cowboys receiver Michael Irvin also brought Beer into the conversation after Herbert was seen driving her to the airport. Irvin questioned the quarterback's priorities following the Chargers' loss to Las Vegas.Interestingly, Herbert's own public comments don't fit the negative social-media narrative. After the couple announced their engagement in July, Herbert spoke warmly about Beer during training camp, saying she had “changed my life” and describing finding someone to spend his life with as an incredible feeling.The couple made their engagement public in July 2026 after roughly a year of dating. So while fans are now debating whether Beer represents a distraction, Herbert himself has publicly described the relationship in very different terms.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Elbow surgery 'not on the table' for QB Jayden Daniels right now, Commanders GM Adam Peters says
articles.summary: Peters also told 106.7 The Fan in Washington on Friday morning that the team hasn't discussed placing Daniels on injured reserve.
articles.body:
Elbow surgery is "not on the table" at the moment for Jayden Daniels , and the Washington Commanders haven't discussed placing the third-year quarterback on injured reserve, general manager Adam Peters said Friday morning during an appearance on 106.7 The Fan in Washington.

But, as was the case that time, Daniels didn't sustain a fracture to his non-throwing arm. He missed four weeks, yet only three games, last season while nursing his dislocated left elbow. That said, he re-injured himself in his first game back , while running to make a tackle after throwing an interception in Week 14 versus the Minnesota Vikings and then was shut down for the remainder of the 2025 campaign.

Daniels had been meeting with specialists to learn more about his injury this week . On Friday, Peters told "The Junkies" on 106.7 The Fan that Daniels returned Thursday night.

"The guys are meeting with him this morning, and we met with doctors, like we said, all over the country, and it was very thorough, and we really got a lot of good opinions," Peters said. "So now it's just a matter of sitting down and thinking about what the best course of action is. But, as of right now, surgery is not on the table, and we haven't discussed IR. So it's just a matter of how we're going to get him back on the field, and that's still to be determined."

"The guys are meeting with him this morning, and we met with doctors, like we said, all over the country, and it was very thorough, and we really got a lot of good opinions," Peters said.

"So now it's just a matter of sitting down and thinking about what the best course of action is. But, as of right now, surgery is not on the table, and we haven't discussed IR. So it's just a matter of how we're going to get him back on the field, and that's still to be determined."

That evaluation hints that Daniels will be back out there within four weeks, considering that landing on IR costs a player a minimum of four games.

Not long after Peters' appearance on 106.7 The Fan, ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Friday that Daniels won't be placed on IR and will be considered "week-to-week."

Although the 25-year-old Daniels has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Seahawks, Washington is hoping the 2024 NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year comes back as soon as possible.

Daniels will wear a brace over his left elbow, according to The MMQB's Albert Breer, who also reported Friday that, because the Commanders are traveling overseas for their Week 4 matchup with the Indianapolis Colts , they'll be leaving on Tuesday night for that trip to London, meaning they'll have to decide imminently if Daniels is joining them.

Regarding Daniels' timeline, Peters was asked on 106.7 The Fan if it comes down to Daniels making the call.

"You're always going to lean on your medical team on that, and it's a medical decision," Peters said . "Every injury is different. And so some of it's you're unable to play, some of it's there's a ramp-up period or a return-to-play timeline. "And then a lot of it's just, on some injuries, can you play? So there's all those different things that factor into it, and that's what we're working through right now."

"You're always going to lean on your medical team on that, and it's a medical decision," Peters said . "Every injury is different. And so some of it's you're unable to play, some of it's there's a ramp-up period or a return-to-play timeline.

"And then a lot of it's just, on some injuries, can you play? So there's all those different things that factor into it, and that's what we're working through right now."

Marcus Mariota , the No. 2 overall selection in the NFL Draft nine years before Daniels went off the board at that spot, will continue to fill the void.

Mariota, 32, is now in his third season with the Commanders. He started eight games in place of Daniels last season and made 11 total appearances, clocking out with 10 touchdown passes, 7 picks and 297 rushing yards.

In relief of Daniels against the Cowboys last week, Mariota hit on 11-of-16 attempts for 111 yards and one touchdown.

"I think the world of Marcus as a human being but also as a leader," Peters said Friday on 106.7 The Fan . "To me, he's the best backup quarterback in the league. And you can argue that, but, in my eyes, seeing what he does day in and day out here, seeing how he performs at practice, seeing how he leads in his own way, we have a lot of confidence in him.

"Our offense has a lot of confidence in him. The whole team has a lot of confidence in him. And I think we can still run our whole offense. We can still do everything we need to do with Marcus. And, so, that's why we have him. And I feel really good about him moving forward. However long we need him, I know Marcus can help us get wins."

articles.title: How Patrick Mahomes turned $400,000 and 8 acres of nothing into an $8 million dream home
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes didn't buy a mansion. He built one, from scratch, on empty land, in the middle of nowhere outside Kansas City.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes didn't buy a mansion. He built one, from scratch, on empty land, in the middle of nowhere outside Kansas City. In September 2020, fresh off signing his record-breaking 10-year, $503 million contract extension, Mahomes and his wife, Brittany, quietly bought an 8-acre plot in Belton, Missouri. It was just trees and dirt. No house, no driveway, nothing. The price tag? A modest $400,000, pocket change for a guy who'd just become the highest-paid athlete in American sports history. Three years, one Netflix docuseries, and a small fortune in construction later, that empty lot is now a private compound worth an estimated $8 million.Mahomes said he built "the exact house" he wanted, and he wasn't lyingThe story of the property began in 2020, when Mahomes purchased an undeveloped eight-acre parcel in Belton, Missouri, shortly after signing his massive contract extension with the Chiefs. Rather than buying an existing mansion and renovating it, the quarterback decided to create the home he wanted from scratch."I actually decided to get the land, to get ready to build that right when I signed my contract here in Kansas City," Mahomes said on Netflix'sQuarterback."I knew I wanted to be here. So when I did that, I was like, 'I'mma be here, I might as well build the exact house I want.'" That decision eventually produced a custom-built compound that the Mahomes family moved into in 2023. Architectural Digest reported that Mahomes bought the land because he knew he wanted to remain in Kansas City and wanted to build a home specifically around his family's lifestyle.The property has since become one of the most talked-about athlete homes in the Kansas City area.There is a football field in the backyardThe most obvious sign that this is Patrick Mahomes' house is sitting right outside it. The estate has a private 50-yard football field complete with Mahomes' personal logo at midfield and his surname across an end zone. It is essentially a miniature version of the environment Mahomes spends his professional life in. Instead of driving to a practice facility to throw a few passes, the Chiefs star can walk outside.And then there is the golf holeIf football isn't enough, Mahomes can apparently switch sports without leaving home. The estate includes a par-3 golf hole, complete with its own green and surrounding water. Aerial footage of the property makes the scale particularly obvious. The golf area stretches out alongside the mansion, while the football field occupies another huge section of the grounds.There is also a private pond, giving the property an almost resort-like appearance from above. Architectural Digest previously highlighted the par-three hole, pond and football field among the estate's standout outdoor features.The indoor basketball court takes things up another levelThe Mahomes family did not stop with outdoor sports. Inside the property is a full indoor basketball court. The space has also been used for family celebrations. Architectural Digest reported that the court was transformed into a football-themed party space for Mahomes' son Bronze's first birthday, complete with football-related decorations and picnic areas.A pool that looks straight out of a resortThe backyard doesn't exactly scream “quiet suburban home.” A large swimming pool sits alongside the mansion, surrounded by outdoor entertainment areas. The estate also features a swim-up bar and firepit, according to Architectural Digest.Inside, Mahomes has his own football museumOne of the property's standout interior features is a display area for Mahomes' collection of trophies and memorabilia. There is also an enormous built-in aquarium and bar in one of the home's reception areas. And then comes perhaps the most personal room in the house: Mahomes' closet.The quarterback has long been known for his sneaker collection, and his custom home includes a boutique-style walk-in closet designed to showcase his shoes and other accessories.Even the movie theater has a Mahomes twistA home theater would already be an impressive feature. Mahomes apparently decided it needed some personality. The theater is reportedly decorated with his numbered jerseys and cleats, turning what could have been a standard luxury-home movie room into another reminder of his NFL career.The property was built around Mahomes' life in Kansas CityMahomes has also maintained a luxury home in the Dallas-Fort Worth area for the offseason, but the Missouri property carries a different significance because it was created after he committed his long-term future to Kansas City. Architectural Digest noted that Mahomes bought the land in 2020 and built the home specifically because he knew he wanted to remain in the area.And that explains why the house feels so unusually personal. articles.title: Tom Brady's marriage to Gisele Bündchen ended with three brutal words

articles.body: Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen's marriage appeared to be hanging by a thread in the months before their 2022 divorce, but according to a new book, the final breaking point may have been far more unexpected than their long-running disagreements over football. The former power couple had reportedly reached a stage where they were still speaking regularly and trying to work through their problems. Brady would FaceTime Bündchen during the day between meetings, checking in and asking if she needed anything. But what exactly happened that broke the couple entirely?Gisele had reportedly been unhappy with Brady's football career for yearsFrom the outside, things appeared to be improving. Then came an alleged conversation that left Brady blindsided.According to an eyewitness quoted in Lars Anderson's new biography Brady: An American Story and the Price of Greatness, Bündchen, who was deeply interested in astrology, looked to the stars and came to a blunt conclusion about their relationship.She allegedly told Brady: “We're not compatible.” And, according to the source, that was it.The revelation came after years of tension surrounding Brady's decision to continue playing in the NFL. Bündchen had reportedly wanted more of her husband at home, particularly as the couple raised their two children, Benjamin and Vivian. She also helped raise Brady's eldest son, Jack, whom he shares with actress Bridget Moynahan.The couple's struggles allegedly became particularly apparent after Brady's sixth Super Bowl victory in 2017. Moments after Brady led the New England Patriots to a stunning comeback against the Atlanta Falcons, Bündchen ran onto the field with their children to celebrate.But according to Anderson's book, her first question for Brady was not about his historic victory. She asked whether it might finally be time for him to retire.Brady reportedly avoided answering.Later that night, Bündchen allegedly raised the subject again. When Brady finally responded, he reportedly told her: “Too bad, babe. I'm having too much fun right now.”The issue did not disappear. The couple announced their divorce on October 28, 2022, ending 13 years of marriage.The exact private circumstances surrounding their split remain known only to Brady and Bündchen. Anderson's account relies on interviews with people who knew the couple and events surrounding their marriage, while the former couple themselves have previously described their divorce more broadly as the result of growing apart.Still, if the account in the book is accurate, the final conversation was strikingly simple: after years of arguments over football, family and time together, three words allegedly delivered the final blow: “We're not compatible.”Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: NFLPA says field in Brazil still needs repairs before Week 3 Cowboys-Ravens Rio game, citing traction and stability issues
articles.summary: Experts from the NFL and NFLPA recommended the field at Rio de Janeiro's Maracanã Stadium needs to be reinforced to provide better stability for players.
articles.body:
Amid concerns about the playing conditions for Week 3's NFL international Rio game between the Dallas Cowboys and Baltimore Ravens , the NFL Players Association explained what its biggest issues are regarding the field at Brazil's Maracanã Stadium, which has been soaked by record rainfall during the late summer.

NFLPA executive director JC Tretter posted a lengthy statement on social media, including what has needed to be addressed with the grass playing surface in Rio de Janeiro leading up to kickoff on Sunday.

"The concern heading into this week was that the field would be loose, patchy, and lead to excessive slipping," Tretter wrote. "Those conditions are generally more of a playability and performance issue than a significant injury concern."

Tretter added that safety is the primary issue for players. But a surface that allows them to perform at their highest level, resulting in a well-played game, is also a major consideration.

Both the league and experts hired by the NFLPA have checked the field during the past week and found that the grass surface wasn't stable enough to be suitable for a game.

"Both the NFLPA's and the league's field experts have been on the ground in Brazil for days, monitoring conditions and working to make the surface as safe and playable as possible for Sunday," Tretter continued . "Based on our experts' assessment, the field needed better traction and stability," he explained. "They recommended reinforced stitching to help the surface hold together and brought in equipment to reinforce as much of the field as possible before the game. Our experts will remain engaged and continue evaluating conditions through kickoff."

"They recommended reinforced stitching to help the surface hold together and brought in equipment to reinforce as much of the field as possible before the game. Our experts will remain engaged and continue evaluating conditions through kickoff."

NFLPA says Brazil field issues highlight larger concerns for league

The NFLPA followed up worries over the playing conditions at Maracanã Stadium to highlight additional concerns that the league needs to address, citing the high temperatures of the artificial surface at Nashville's Nissan Stadium during Week 2's game between the Philadelphia Eagles and Tennessee Titans .

As the game progressed, the temperature of the artificial turf reached 157 degrees, according to the Fox broadcast. Eagles offensive lineman Cam Jurgens told reporters that he needed to replace multiple pairs of his cleats because of the hot surface. Fox cameras showed Titans players having their cleats watered down to cool them off.

"We need field standards that account for both safety and performance," Tretter wrote. "The NFL, NFLPA, and our field and engineering experts spend a lot of time working on these issues, and we've made progress. But we're not where we need to be yet."

Tretter also said the conditions in Brazil demonstrate that the NFL needs to slow down its ambitions for international expansion if field conditions can't be made suitable for one showcase game, let alone an entire eight- or nine-game home schedule.

"Two of the three games played in Brazil have had field-related issues. That's not a coincidence," he pointed out. "This time of year makes it extremely challenging to maintain the kind of grass surface we expect at the NFL level."

Tretter ended his statement by saying the players want the NFL game to grow internationally, but not at the cost of safety and high standards for playing conditions.

The NFL Rio game will kick off at 4:25 p.m. ET Sunday and be televised on CBS.

articles.title: NFL wife fires back at league over ridiculous 15k fine, Presidents Cup has no juice & CBS's Melanie Collins!
articles.summary: The final Friday of September brings Kristin Juszczyk and Kyle Juszczyk trolling Roger Goodell over the NFL's absurd $14,926 celebration fine.
articles.body: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com. Final Friday of September. It's true. I had to double-check it, but it's true. We're six days away from October. Goodness. Weren't we just grilling burgers on Labor Day Monday? What happened here? Wild stuff. The good news? October is, objectively speaking, the best month of the entire year. It's really not even close. MLB playoffs. Football in full swing. Hockey starts back up. Still no NBA. The best. It's what I hope heaven is like. On that note, welcome to a Friday Nightcaps — the one where Kristin Juszczyk teams up with her 49ers husband, Kyle, to send a stern message to Roger Goodell and the No Fun League (NFL). NFL FINES PLAYER NICKNAMED 'JUICE' $14,926 FOR USING A DRINKING CELEBRATION, CALLING IT OFFENSIVE What a stunt they pulled earlier this week. They have absolutely no shame. You'll see. What else should we hit on today before we leave early because it's a Football Friday and there are five (!!!) college football games today? I've got NFL on CBS sideline reporter Melanie Collins checking in before Week 3, Al Michaels didn't have the greatest night in the booth last night, and Wyndham Clark wasn't a fan of the ... fans ... at the Presidents Cup in Thursday's opening round. I don't blame him, by the way. But also, this event ain't exactly the Ryder Cup. Never has been, and never will be. There's just no juice in it. OK, grab you ... some juice! ... and settle in for a Friday 'Cap: Kristin Juszczyk takes the $15k fine in stride We ended yesterday's class with the dumbest story in the NFL ... maybe ever? For those who missed it, Roger Goodell's Fun Police fined 49ers FB Kyle Juszczyk a whopping $14,926 for celebrating a touchdown by giving the universal symbol of taking a drink. The league took it as Juszczyk "chugging a beer," according to the letter sent to Juszczyk. That violates Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1, which, frankly, sounds like the dumbest rule of all time. Anyway, the Niners star has been doing that celebration for years, and it has nothing to do with beer. He barely drinks beer. Instead, it's an homage to his nickname — "Juice." By the way, as OutKick's Armando Salguero noted, Juszczyk scored the tuddy, did his VERY BAD celebration, and then the first commercial that appeared when FOX went to break? A Michelob Ultra ad. Amazing. We all caught up now? Good! Now, let's check in with Kyle's wife, Kristin, who had her husband join her for an Instagram message to the league: Does anyone care about the Presidents Cup? "Kyle’s got a drinking problem," the caption says, followed by the little nod to the league with the text in the video that reads, "$14,926 glass of juice." Amazing. It really is a ridiculous fine by the league, and my bar for Goodell is already so low. The NFL has been the No Fun League for decades now. You can't celebrate. You can't taunt. You can't hit the QB. You can't touch the receiver. God forbid you jump on the goal posts after you score a touchdown. I'm fairly certain that celebration is punishable by death at this point. But this fine ... for a DRINKING GESTURE ... might just be the leader in the clubhouse. It's that silly. Especially when all the league promotes is drinking and gambling. That's literally every single commercial on NFL Sundays. That's it. Bud Light and Kalshi. And Jason Kelce hosting a football party, of course. Can't forget that one. Anyway, good for Kristin for fighting back. It pays to have an influencer wife, you know? Yep. That works! OK, let's move this class along and check in with Wyndham Clark and Team USA: Al, Melanie & Doug's rant "It was kind of dead out there. I felt like the momentum could have been better, to be honest, because we weren’t really feeling the fans, I think, as much as normal. There was a few shots — I mean, Collin hit a 5-wood on, what was it, 11 to like 10 feet, and we didn’t even know if it was on the green because no one clapped. It was a little surprising." I don't love Wyndham Clark, but it's tough to argue with him here. I said it on Monday ... I had NO idea the Presidents Cup was this week. None. Zero. It's been the least-hyped golf event of my lifetime. They played all day yesterday and I didn't see one thing about it on social media. Not one. I know this has always been the little brother to the Ryder Cup, but it's been as bad as I can remember this year. And now we're going into the weekend and putting it up against college football and the NFL? Good luck. Not great! OK, let's rapid-fire this Friday class into a big weekend. First up? How do we feel about Al's performance last night? Thoughts? The confusion on the "ATL" chants were wild, from both guys. How were they so bewildered by "ATL" chants ... when the ATLanta Falcons were playing? What do you guys think "ATL" means?! Feel like that one comes with some pretty easy context clues. It wasn't his best. The good news? It's only Week 3. Come on, Al! Chin up, and let's turn this season around. Next? On the way out, here's Doug Gottlieb going on what I thought was relatively solid 5-minute rant on the current state of college athletics: I'm not the biggest Gottlieb fan, but I actually agree with a lot of what he says there. The free-for-all that is the transfer portal has gotten laughably out of control in college sports, specifically football and basketball. It's just insane. To me, that's the worst part of this whole NIL era we're suffering through right now. I can stomach the ridiculous amounts of money being thrown at these 18-year-olds. But seeing a 23-year-old on his 5th team in as many years just ruins the whole experience. OK, that's it for today — and this week. Good work, everyone. Another weekend is here. articles.title: Puka Nacua, Malik Nabers, NFL Injury Statuses and Fantasy Impact for Week 3
articles.summary: Puka Nacua will likely miss his second straight game of the early 2026 NFL season.
articles.body:
Puka Nacua will likely miss his second straight game of the early 2026 NFL season.

The Los Angeles Rams wide receiver is listed as doubtful for his team's Week 3 clash with the Denver Broncos.

The news is much better for Malik Nabers, who is on track to play for the New York Giants on Sunday.

Schefter Talks Possible Giants QB Targets

Nabers' health might be the least of the concerns for fantasy football players with him on the roster since Jameis Winston didn't look great in backup duty for the injured Jaxson Dart on Monday.

Below is a look at all of the significant injury news affecting fantasy football matchups in Week 3.

Puka Nacua has a doubtful designation for Week 3.

Nacua did not practice on Friday due to the hip and groin injuries that forced him out of Week 2, per ESPN's Sarah Barshop.

ESPN's Adam Schefter noted, though, that Nacua could return as early as Week 4.

The Rams offense thrived in Nacua's absence in Week 2. Davante Adams had eight catches, 195 yards and two touchdowns. Terrance Ferguson recorded 54 yards and a score off six catches.

Ferguson is the better waiver-wire pickup of the two since Adams was widely drafted across most fantasy leagues.

No other Rams player had more than two catches in Week 2. It's not worth taking the risk with wide receivers further down the depth chart in a tough matchup with Denver.

Adonai Mitchell of the New York Jets and Houston's Jaylin Noel are two under-the-radar selections for Week 3.

The Jets and Texans face the Detroit Lions and Indianapolis Colts, respectively, who both have top-five pass-yard concessions in the NFL.

Mitchell has had as many targets as Garrett Wilson through two weeks, while Noel is second on the Texans in receiving yards.

Buffalo's Khalil Shakir and Keon Coleman are replacement options for Nacua as well. The high-flying Bills offense faces an struggling Los Angeles Chargers team at home on Sunday.

Malik Nabers was a full participant in New York Giants practice on Thursday.

That was a big step in the right direction for the star wide receiver, who hurt his shoulder on Monday night in Los Angeles.

Nabers shouldn't have any injury concerns going into Week 3's home clash with the Tennessee Titans.

On paper, Nabers has an excellent matchup against one of the league's worst teams, but he needs Jameis Winston to be better in order to take full advantage of the Titans' defense.

Winston went 11-for-27 with 111 yards in relief duty on Monday night after Jaxson Dart went down with what turned out to be a season-ending knee injury.

New York's matchup is significantly easier against the Titans than it was versus the Rams. That's one of the primary reasons to trust the Giants to put up big numbers on Sunday.

DeVonta Smith eclipsed the 100-yard mark last week against the Titans and Garrett Wilson had 79 yards on six catches in Week 1.

The early precedent set by the Titans defense is that No. 1 wide receivers can feast against them. The hope for Nabers is that trend continues into Week 3, even with a backup quarterback tossing him the ball.

articles.title: Bears Announce Caleb Williams, 8 More Injury Updates Before Eagles Game
articles.summary: The Bears announced injury updates on Caleb Williams and eight more players before their game against the Eagles, clarifying their latest status. The post Be...
articles.body:
Injured quarterback Caleb Williams didn't practice Friday, and the Chicago Bears ' Friday practice before hosting the Philadelphia Eagles gave no hint that his status will change by kickoff Monday night.

That leaves coach Ben Johnson's offense trusting a stopgap quarterback against a Philadelphia defense already sniffing an opening, with Soldier Field waiting for 38-year-old Case Keenum to take the first snap.

The Bears' Friday update, the second of three weekly filings due before Monday Night Football against Philadelphia, listed Williams as a non-participant for the second straight day with the hamstring injury that cut short last Sunday's outing.

Johnson does not expect Williams to practice at all this week and has stopped short of ruling him out, according to ChicagoBears.com's Larry Mayer, though nobody around the building treats Monday as likely.

Backup Tyson Bagent isn't in much better shape. He entered the NFL's concussion protocol after relieving Williams last Sunday, missed Wednesday's session at Halas Hall entirely, and returned Friday only to sit out again.

Bagent has yet to clear the protocol, according to NBC Sports , leaving Keenum as the only healthy quarterback on Chicago's 53-man roster.

*The Chicago Bears did not practice on Thursday; participation was an estimation. ^ Reserve/PUP — 21-day practice window.

Caleb Williams Update Anchors Crowded Injury Report

Kicker Cairo Santos is a new concern, sitting out for a second straight day with a right hip injury. Chicago carries no backup kicker, meaning a trip to the free agent market becomes likely if Santos can't answer the bell, according to the Chicago Sun-Times .

The news wasn't all bad. Running back Kyle Monangai returned to full participation after sitting out Thursday with a knee issue, according to The Athletic's Kevin Fishbain — the clearest positive of the week. With D'Andre Swift healthy and left off the report entirely, Chicago's two-back rotation looks intact regardless of who throws them the ball.

Cornerback Tyrique Stevenson upgraded from a non-participant to limited with his hamstring injury, still short of clearance. Defensive lineman Shemar Turner and linebacker Noah Sewell remained limited after their physically unable to perform 21-day practice windows opened Wednesday, according to ChicagoBears.com — a step toward eligibility, not permission to play. Guard Joe Thuney 's absence was a scheduled rest day.

Left tackle Ozzy Trapilo , working without restrictions in full pads, didn't appear on the report, positioning him to stabilize the line in front of whichever passer starts. Cornerback Kyler Gordon remains on the physically unable to perform list working off-site, according to ESPN's team injury tracker .

What Chicago Bears' Report Signals for Eagles Chances

The report points toward a conservative approach — control the football, lean on the run and ask a limited passing game to avoid mistakes.

The bigger question sits on defense, where Stevenson's limited hamstring and Gordon's absence push more snaps toward less experienced cornerbacks against the Eagles attack.

The betting market has noticed. Philadelphia is favored by 3 1/2 points with the total sitting near 43 1/2, according to Covers.com , numbers that fit a backup-quarterback, run-first night better than a shootout.

Santos remains the wild card. A missed kick or a shortened field-goal range could swing a game many expect to stay low-scoring. Saturday's injury designations are expected to settle the quarterback and kicker questions.

articles.title: Iowa quarterback Hank Brown leads #17 Hawkeyes into Saturday’s matchup at #18 Michigan
articles.summary: IOWA CITY, Iowa (KCAU) – There’s plenty to credit for a 3-0 start for the Iowa Hawkeyes as they moved up to #17 in the newest AP Poll. Iowa’s defense has all...
articles.body:
IOWA CITY, Iowa (KCAU) - There's plenty to credit for a 3-0 start for the Iowa Hawkeyes as they moved up to #17 in the newest AP Poll.

Iowa's defense has allowed only 13 points all season, but a big key has been the Hawkeye offense led by quarterback Hank Brown .

Brown has paced the Hawkeyes to a scorching 37 points per game through the team's first three contests as the senior has been efficient, boasting 473 passing yards and three touchdowns with a completion percentage of 72.6%.

The senior looks to continue rolling as the Hawkeyes begin Big Ten play with a visit to fellow unbeaten and #18 Michigan on Saturday as Iowa aims for its first win in 'The Big House' since 2010.

Brown feels he's learned more as the season progressed and looks to apply those lessons heading into conference play.

"Playing quarterback in the game of football you're never going to be super comfortable and there's always going to be different things that the defense is going to throw at you, and the ball bounces a different way sometimes. But just being able to continue to be efficient and lean on the guys around me, I've got some studs around me and an awesome offensive line, so I am comfortable knowing those guys are going to make plays for me ans we're going to have fun while we're doing it," Brown said.

Iowa and Michigan kick off on Saturday at 2:30 p.m.

articles.title: ‘Don’t Think He’s With the Team Next Year’ — Browns Insider Makes Bold Shedeur Sanders Prediction Amid Lost Deshaun Watson QB Battle
articles.summary: Shedeur Sanders has been the topic of discussion ever since the Cleveland Browns chose Deshaun Watson over him for the starting quarterback position. The dec...
articles.body:
Shedeur Sanders has been the topic of discussion ever since the Cleveland Browns chose Deshaun Watson over him for the starting quarterback position.

The decision was made by Browns head coach Todd Monken after an intense training camp competition. Fans and analysts have been questioning Sanders' future with the organization after the decision went against him.

Tony Grossi Predicts Shedeur Sanders ' Browns Exit

In a recent episode of ESPN Cleveland , analyst Tony Grossi shared his point of view when asked about Sanders' future with the organization . He said:

"How does Shedeur Sanders' tenure in Cleveland end? This is torture. He's not going to be on the team next year. Can we all agree with that? I don't know that. Oh, I think I do know that. I don't know that. See, anything I say is going to sound like I want this to happen, and that's not what you're asking me. You're asking me what I think will happen. I don't think he's with the team next year. Okay. Why? Because I think they have Taylen Green . I think they have Dillon Gabriel . I think they have a rookie. And I think they look at a mid-price little bridge veteran, veteran quarterback. Okay, so I think he's the odd man out."

The competition between Watson and Sanders was head-to-head. Both quarterbacks were given alternating reps by head coach Todd Monken during the competition, giving each of them an opportunity to prove themselves and make a case for the starting position.

With the quarterback battle now settled, questions remain about where Sanders fits into Cleveland's plans moving forward. Grossi's comments are his personal assessment of what he believes could happen and do not represent an official decision from the Browns. Sanders could still have opportunities to prove himself during the season, particularly if he gets a chance to take meaningful snaps.

For Sanders, the coming season could eventually play an important role in determining his future with the organization. If he is able to show that he is the right fit for the Browns, the head coach might give him a second thought and reconsider his position within the team. His performance, development, and ability to take advantage of any opportunities could all become important factors when Cleveland evaluates its quarterback room moving forward.

The Browns will have several decisions to make when the season comes to an end, and the quarterback room could look different in the future. For now, Sanders remains with Cleveland, and there has been no official announcement that the organization plans to move on from him. Grossi's prediction has therefore added another storyline to an already closely watched quarterback situation.

articles.title: Browns news: Why Todd Monken still has 'huge belief' in Deshaun Watson

articles.body:
Todd Monken continues to affirm his support for Deshaun Watson as the Cleveland Browns quarterback regains his form throughout the 2026 NFL season.

Monken started his first year as the Browns' head coach, off to a 1-1 start two games in. He named Watson as the starting quarterback over Shedeur Sanders , believing the former can return to star form and help Cleveland win games.

Despite Watson's controversy and season-ending injuries in past years, Monken appeared on the Pat McAfee Show to explain why he maintains belief in the quarterback .

"I have a huge belief in all of our players, especially Deshaun, because I've seen it. Now, had he been away from the game for a while, yes, and playing only whatever it was, 19 games over five years. That's going to sting not only his confidence level but also, system-wise, like, who is he? And all I saw was a guy that just continued to work," Monken said.

"He had no reason to work over the last 22 months to come back. He had all the money was guaranteed for God's sakes. I mean, shoot, he'd already had a heck of a career, but for him to come back and work like he did [is great]…I was happy for him all the work he put in because isn't that why we do it? Don't we do this for our players to try and create the best version of our players that we can and show belief in them and then let the chips fall where they may."

What lies ahead for Deshaun Watson , Browns

Deshaun Watson has delivered a solid performance to lead the Browns to their first win of 2026. It's the first step to what can present potential for a rebuilding Cleveland squad.

Two games into 2026, Watson has completed 40 out of 52 passes for 443 yards and three touchdowns and one interception. Cleveland is 1-1 after losing to Jacksonville then beating Tampa Bay.

articles.title: Sam Darnold Injury Return Hyped as 'Medical Miracle' by Seahawks HC After Initial Timetable
articles.summary: Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald was impressed with the speed at which quarterback Sam Darnold recovered from a glute injury.
articles.body:
Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald was impressed with the speed at which quarterback Sam Darnold recovered from a glute injury.

"Really just to see him confident in the things that he's been doing," Macdonald said Friday, according to ESPN's Brady Henderson . "He's been really positive and says he feels great. He looks great, so we'll rolling. It's a medical miracle he's back."

He also explained that the quarterback's timetable had "shifted quite drastically" for the better after Week 2, per Henderson.

Darnold's injury occurred on Seattle's opening drive of a Week 1 victory over the New England Patriots. He's now set to return for the Seahawks' matchup with the Washington Commanders on Sunday.

On Thursday, Darnold revealed that he feared his season might be over and his long-term career could be impacted immediately after suffering the injury (via Henderson).

NFL insider Tom Pelissero previously reported the Seahawks were initially worried that Darnold fractured his hip socket, which would have been a major injury.

Now, he'll only miss one week of action before returning to the defending Super Bowl champions.

The Seahawks have still started 2-0 largely due to the efforts of backup quarterback Drew Lock, who has completed 72.9 percent of his throws for 422 yards and four touchdowns without getting picked off this year.

Darnold's first game back will come against a Commanders defense that has struggled to begin the 2026 season, ranking No. 27 among all teams by allowing 30.5 points per game.

Kickoff between Seattle and Washington on Sunday is at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: In 1990, a car accident nearly killed Brett Favre before he ever threw an NFL pass; 3 decades later, the game is still sorting out how to remember a man who gave it everything and broke its heart
articles.summary: Brett Favre was 20 years old when a car crash on a rural Mississippi road left him with a 30-inch scar, a removed portion of his small intestine, and the
articles.body: Brett Favre was 20 years old when a car crash on a rural Mississippi road left him with a 30-inch scar, a removed portion of his small intestine, and the kind of near-death moment that resets a person. He survived. He went on to throw 508 NFL touchdowns. He won a Super Bowl. He played through pain that would have sidelined most mortals. And then, in the years that followed his retirement, he made choices that have left the league genuinely unsure what to do with him.What happened to Brett Favre in the 1990 car accident?The summer of 1990 was not supposed to be the summer Brett Favre almost died. He was a 20-year-old college quarterback at Southern Miss, heading home. The car left the road, rolled, and when everything stopped moving, Favre was airlifted to a hospital in critical condition. Doctors removed 30 inches of his small intestine. He lost 34 pounds. And two months later, he was back on a football field.That story became foundational to the Favre mythology. Toughness. Resilience. A guy you just could not keep down. He played 297 consecutive regular-season games. He won three straight MVP awards. He dragged the Green Bay Packers to a Super Bowl title in 1996 and turned a franchise city into a religious experience for an entire generation of fans. There was something almost ridiculous about his durability, the way he played through a broken thumb, a sprained ankle, a torn ligament, sometimes all in the same season.But the mythology always sat on a more complicated foundation. The addiction to painkillers was real. His retirement-and-unretirement cycle wore out multiple front offices and created genuine damage in Minnesota, where his late-career run with the Vikings strained relationships that had been decades in the making. And then, long after the jersey was hung up, came the welfare fund scandal in Mississippi. Favre was accused of directing millions in state welfare funds toward projects that personally benefited him, including a volleyball facility at the university where his daughter played. He has denied knowingly doing anything wrong. The legal proceedings are ongoing.The NFL, for its part, has mostly stayed quiet. His bust is in Canton. His number is retired in Green Bay. But the league that once celebrated him on every highlight reel has grown noticeably quieter about the Favre brand in recent years.How is the NFL remembering Brett Favre now, more than a decade after his retirement?There is no clean answer, which is part of what makes this so uncomfortable for everyone involved. The Hall of Fame does not have a mechanism for revisionism. His records stand. The memories of those Monday night performances, those frozen-field moments, those throws that no rational quarterback should have attempted, those are not going anywhere.What has shifted is the tone. The NFL networks do not loop Favre content the way they once did. His appearances at league events have thinned. And within Green Bay, a city that made him a near-deity, there is a genuine and sometimes painful conversation happening about legacy versus accountability.Brett Favre himself has spoken about his health in recent years, revealing that he has been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease. He has also become more vocal about the dangers of head trauma in football, a subject he admits he did not think much about while he was playing through every hit. That part of his story carries a different kind of weight now.What remains is a player who was, for a stretch of years in the 1990s, the most compelling figure in American sport. The guy who survived a crash at 20 and then played football like he had something to prove every single Sunday. The NFL has not figured out how to square that with what came after. articles.title: In 2003, NFL legend Drew Bledsoe quietly purchased 80 acres of Washington vineyard land; years later, his Doubleback winery had grown to 450 acres and 70 employees, earning a Wine Spectator Top 100 ranking
articles.summary: Most NFL quarterbacks spend their final seasons worried about their completion percentage. Drew Bledsoe was thinking about cabernet sauvignon.
articles.body: Most NFL quarterbacks spend their final seasons worried about their completion percentage. Drew Bledsoe was thinking about cabernet sauvignon. While still under contract with the Buffalo Bills in 2003, he bought 80 acres of vineyard land in Walla Walla, Washington, the small farming town he grew up in. Nobody made much of it at the time. Years later, that quiet land purchase had grown into Doubleback, a winery sitting on 450 acres with 70 full-time employees and a Wine Spectator Top 100 ranking under its belt.Why did Drew Bledsoe start a winery after his NFL career?Drew Bledsoe's path to wine did not start at retirement. It started much earlier, in a farmland town that most people outside Washington state would not recognize on a map. Growing up in Walla Walla, he was surrounded by agriculture. The valley's summers were hot, the nights cool, and the soil had a texture that winemakers had been quietly excited about for years.He had started developing a taste for wine during his NFL years, sharing bottles with teammates and their families after games. It grew from a casual interest into something more deliberate. By 2003, with retirement somewhere on the horizon, he made his first move, purchasing the land that would eventually become the McQueen Vineyard."When you look at facing retirement in your mid-30s, and all of a sudden the outlet for that passion and work ethic goes away, you can't just sit back in a rocking chair and be retired at 35," Bledsoe said. "I'm not a good enough golfer to play golf every day."That honesty says a lot. Bledsoe was not chasing a vanity project or a tax write-off. He was looking for something that demanded the same competitive energy that football had required of him for 14 years. Wine, it turned out, had plenty of that.How did Doubleback winery become one of Washington's most respected labels?When Drew Bledsoe officially retired in 2007, he returned to Walla Walla and launched Doubleback the following year alongside his wife Maura. The name was deliberate. It was a reference to coming home, to circling back to the place that shaped him before professional football pulled him away. He brought in winemaker Josh McDaniels, who had been working at the respected Figgins Family Wine Estates, to lead production.The early skepticism from the wine community was predictable. Greg Harrington, owner of Gramercy Cellars and one of Walla Walla's most recognized winemakers, admitted he was not exactly impressed when he first heard a former pro athlete was setting up shop nearby. "My first thought was, 'Yeah, just what we need,'" Harrington said. "Some former pro athlete who knows nothing about wine."That skepticism did not last. Doubleback's first vintage, a 2007 cabernet sauvignon blend, landed a Wine Spectator Top 100 ranking straight out of the gate. Bottles were priced between $90 and $120, and they sold. The winery was not trying to compete on affordability. It was competing on quality, and the critics noticed.Bledsoe later expanded with Bledsoe Family Winery, a sister label designed to offer more variety at a lower price point. Then came Bledsoe/McDaniels, a collaboration focused on small-lot, single-vineyard wines. What started as one plot of land had quietly grown into a multi-label wine operation.How big has Drew Bledsoe's wine business grown since he left the NFL?The numbers tell a story Drew Bledsoe himself still finds difficult to fully explain. From a single planted vineyard to more than 450 acres and 70 employees, the growth has not been accidental. He has added estate vineyards across the Walla Walla Valley, acquired the àMaurice Vineyard in the Upper Mill Creek area, and extended his reach into Oregon's Eola-Amity Hills, where 80 acres now grow Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, and Chenin Blanc."Early on, we were not thinking that we were going to have three wineries and have 60 employees," Bledsoe admitted. "We were just going to be a cool little boutique winery and hopefully make some good wine."There is something worth noting in that. Bledsoe has never oversold what Doubleback is. He has not put his name on cheap merchandise or chased mass distribution. The investment into the business, which he described as running into the seven figures, was treated with the same seriousness he gave his playing career. It shows in the reputation the label has built."It's been super rewarding to see something grow from a single vineyard that we planted with our hands to a company that has 70 employees and over 450 acres of vineyards," he said.NFL quarterbacks are often defined by what they did under pressure on Sunday afternoons. Bledsoe spent 14 seasons doing exactly that.
