articles.title: Week 3 Waiver Wire Targets to Replace Fantasy Players on Injury List
articles.summary: Injuries have been a major storyline early in the 2026 NFL season, and they've had a significant impact on the fantasy football landscape, too. Things aren't going to change in Week 3.
articles.body:
Injuries have been a major storyline early in the 2026 NFL season, and they've had a significant impact on the fantasy football landscape, too. Things aren't going to change in Week 3.

While fans will see a couple of returning players this week—including Kyler Murray and Michael Penix Jr., who made his 2026 debut on Thursday night—several top fantasy options continue to be sidelined. In the case of New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart, he's done for the season.

Finding viable starters off the waiver wire isn't easy at this point in the week, but a few may still be available in your league. Here, you'll find a look at the latest from the Week 3 injury report , rankings for the top remaining plays on the schedule, and some of those aforementioned late-week targets.

All picks and analysis are based on point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

It appears that Sam Darnold may make his return for the Seattle Seahawks this week. He returned to being a full participant at practice on Thursday, and while he won't rush back before he's ready, Darnold is eager to be back on the playing field.

"I'm really striving for that," Darnold said, per John Boyle of the team's official website.

However, the New York Giants won't have Jaxson Dart, who was placed on injured reserve. The Chicago Bears aren't expected to have Caleb Williams (hamstring) or Tyson Bagent (concussion).

Marcus Mariota will start in place of Jayden Daniels (elbow) this week.

Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young is the top realistic option to target at quarterback this week. He's rostered in 56 percent of leagues but has topped 24 fantasy points in consecutive weeks. He'll face a Cleveland Browns defense that has surrendered an average of 19.5 fantasy points to opposing QBs this week.

Geno Smith, Malik Willis, Jameis Winston, and Mariota are options to consider only in deeper leagues this week.

Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers

There isn't an extensive list of running back injuries, though it's probably worth keeping an eye on Saquon Barkley ahead of Monday night. The Philadelphia Eagles starter suffered a stinger in Week 2 but did practice on Thursday and Friday.

Tennessee Titans back Tyjae Spears is listed as questionable, as is Pittsburgh Steelers running back Jaylen Warren. Rico Dowdle has been ruled out for the Steelers, as has Denver Broncos back Jonah Coleman.

Finding good running backs this season has been difficult, and finding viable options off the wire has been even harder. Kansas City Chiefs backup Emmett Johnson might be the only flex option available in most leagues this week.

Johnson has a clear role behind Kenneth Walker III in Kansas City's offense. It isn't a particularly prominent one, but he does have four catches and 103 scrimmage yards through two weeks. He could see a bigger workload this week if the Chiefs blow out out the Miami Dolphins and spend the second half winding down the clock via the run.

Miami has surrendered the third-most fantasy points to opposing running backs this season.

Tank Bigsby, Emanuel Wilson, Keaton Mitchell, and Mike Washington Jr. are only worth considering in deeper leagues and if desperate.

Several notable receivers have already been ruled out this week, including Nico Collins, Alec Pierce, Caleb Douglas, Andrei Iosivas, and Demarcus Robinson.

The Los Angeles Rams have listed Puka Nacua as doubtful. The Buffalo Bills have listed both Keon Coleman and D.J. Moore as questionable. Jalen Coker, Xavier Legette, Adonai Mitchell, Ryan Miller, Mike Evans, and Michael Pittman Jr. are also listed as questionable.

It's worth checking to see if Browns receiver Denzel Boston is available, as he has caught touchdown passes in back-to-back weeks and is only rostered in 63 percent of fantasy leagues. Las Vegas Raiders receiver Tre Tucker might be a more realistic option from the waiver wire, though.

Tucker, who is rostered in 47 percent of leagues, has caught seven passes for 146 yards and a touchdown through two weeks. Brock Bowers is expected to return for the Raiders this week, but Tucker should still serve as their top perimeter target.

Dontayvion Wicks and Rashod Bateman are other WRs to consider off the wire this week.

As previously mentioned, Bowers (knee) is expected to make his 2026 debut against the New Orleans Saints on Sunday. Officially, he is listed as questionable, as are Eli Raridon and Colby Parkinson. Mason Taylor and Chigoziem Okonkwo are both out.

David Njoku (fibula, IR) and Charlie Kolar (forearm) are both injured for the Los Angeles Chargers, which gives Oronde Gadsden II some TE value this week.

The Chargers will face the Bills, who have surrendered an average of 12.3 fantasy points to opposing tight ends this season. Gadsden is rostered in 26 percent of fantasy leagues.

Terrance Ferguson, Pat Freiermuth, Darren Waller, and T.J. Hockenson are deeper sleepers to consider at tight end.

*Fantasy scoring and roster information from FantasyPros .

articles.title: Re-Ranking Every NFL Team's Quarterback Room Following Jayden Daniels, Jaxson Dart Injuries
articles.summary: Football might be the ultimate team sport, but it's virtually impossible in today's NFL to win consistently without a quality quarterback behind center. This is why teams target signal-callers early in the draft, pay the position more than any other, and spend entire offseasons trying to uncover the best starting options.
articles.body:
Football might be the ultimate team sport, but it's virtually impossible in today's NFL to win consistently without a quality quarterback behind center. This is why teams target signal-callers early in the draft, pay the position more than any other, and spend entire offseasons trying to uncover the best starting options.

Unfortunately, even the best-laid plans won't prevent teams from having to pivot when injuries enter the equation. We've seen some significant ones through the first two weeks of 2026.

On Sunday, Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels suffered his second dislocated elbow in as many seasons. On Wednesday, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo reported that New York Giants starter Jaxson Dart will undergo season-ending knee surgery.

With several quarterback situations already looking quite a bit different than they did ahead of Week 1, let's re-rank every team's QB room based on past performances, recent results, health, depth, and short- and long-term outlooks.

For a look at how quarterbacks performed in Week 2, check out the latest QB report cards from Brent Sobleski of the B/R Scouting Department.

Dart initially appeared to avoid a long-term knee injury after he went down in Week 2. However, further testing revealed a torn meniscus. He was placed on injured reserve.

For now, the Giants will turn to Jameis Winston, a capable backup with a big arm but a penchant for passing to the other team. He isn't the worst quarterback in the league. He went 5-2 as a starter in 2021, but he's gone just 3-9 since and looked overwhelmed (37.7 QB rating) on Monday night.

Jake Haener is on the practice squad and will likely move into a backup role. However, New York will consider adding to its quarterback room.

"All options are open right now," head coach John Harbaugh said, per Christian Arnold of the New York Post .

Unless Winston exceeds the realistic expectations set by his recent play, or the Giants find a new starter, Dart's injury feels like one that could sink their season.

27-year-old quarterback Malik Willis is getting his first real shot at being a full-time NFL starter. His play this season has been acceptable, given the Miami Dolphins' young and below-average supporting cast.

Willis has thrown for 417 yards and one touchdown, with one interception and an 83.5 QB rating. He has also rushed for 45 yards and a score. While he's saddled with an overall lack of talent in Miami and has underwhelming numbers this season, Willis' ceiling remains high, as evidenced by the 134.6 passer rating he posted with the Green Bay Packers.

The depth behind Willis leaves even more to be desired than Willis' 2026 production. Kyle McCord has never seen NFL action. Brady Cook has gone 0-4 as a starter with a 55.4 QB rating.

Second-year quarterback Cam Ward continues to be a work in progress for the Tennessee Titans.

The Titans invested in his supporting cast this offseason, adding pieces like center Austin Schlottmann, receiver Wan'Dale Robinson, and rookie wideout Carnell Tate . They also paired him with an experienced offensive coordinator in Brian Daboll. Yet Ward's development remains slow and steady.

Ward has a pair of rushing touchdowns this season but has thrown for just 323 yards with one touchdown and an 85.7 QB rating. He's on the lower end of the NFL's starting-QB hierarchy right now, though his upside remains high.

Tennessee will undoubtedly be patient with the 2025 first overall pick, but should Ward miss time, the Titans have a 59-game starter (including playoffs) in backup Mitchell Trubisky.

The Pittsburgh Steelers' plan for 2026 was to bring in head coach Mike McCarthy, reunite him with quarterback Aaron Rodgers, and make another playoff run with Rodgers behind center. So far, not so good.

Rodgers played well enough to notch a Week 1 win, but he didn't play well at all in Pittsburgh's Week 2 blowout loss to the New England Patriots. Through two weeks, he's only thrown for 408 yards, one touchdown, one interception, and a 72.1 QB rating.

McCarthy will have to figure out how to get more out of Rodgers and the offense, or else it's going to be a long season in Pittsburgh. The Steelers have an experienced backup in Mason Rudolph (19 starts), but he isn't an upgrade over Rodgers. Will Howard and rookie third-round pick Drew Allar are unproven.

The New York Jets traded for Geno Smith early in the offseason, not to find their offensive savior, but to find someone to steer the ship for a season. Equipped with three 2027 first-round picks, New York will likely go QB hunting in next year's draft.

Smith has been mostly solid through the Jets' 1-1 start, though. He's thrown for only 461 yards and one touchdown, but he's avoided turnovers and posted a solid 95.8 passer rating.

If Smith starts to stumble, the Jets may see what they have in Cade Klubnik . The fourth-round rookie out of Clemson is a bit raw but was once viewed as a potential first-round prospect. New York also recently took a flier on 2023 second-round pick Will Levis by adding him to its practice squad.

The Chicago Bears have one of the NFL's most exciting young signal-callers in Caleb Williams. However, he's dealing with a hamstring injury and is expected to miss some time.

"I'm not putting a timeline on this," head coach Ben Johnson said, per Larry Mayer of the team's official website. "We're going to say week-to-week."

This means the Bears will likely rely on backups in the immediate future. It's looking like QB3 Case Keenum for Week 3, as backup Tyson Bagent is in the concussion protocol.

While Keenum is a very experienced journeyman with 66 starts on his resume, he also hasn't seen regular-season action since 2023. Undrafted Louisville product Miller Moss is on the Bears' practice squad.

Deshaun Watson finally looked like a capable starter, leading the Cleveland Browns to a Week 2 win. However, one above-average performance doesn't erase the four-plus years of poor play and unavailability he's given Cleveland since he arrived.

Now, to be fair, Watson's numbers are solid. He has completed 76.9 percent of his passes for three touchdowns, one interception, and a 112.9 QB rating. However, much of his production in Week 1 came in garbage time. Until he proves he can build on his latest outing, Watson must be considered a lower-tier starter.

If the Browns decide that Watson isn't their best option in 2026, they'll likely turn to 2025 fifth-round pick Shedeur Sanders. He flashed some potential as a rookie but also made his fair share of head-scratching mistakes.

Cleveland also has 2025 third-round pick Dillon Gabriel and rookie Taylen Green on its roster. Green is a very raw prospect, while Sanders and Gabriel went a combined 4-9 as starters last season.

Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett is largely viewed as a placeholder. Whether he's holding down the spot for rookie third-round pick Carson Beck or a top 2027 prospect, though, remains to be seen.

The 33-year-old has been decidedly average so far this season, completing 67.7 percent of his passes for 372 yards, two touchdowns, an interception, and an 86.2 QB rating. While "average" was enough for Arizona to notch a Week 1 win, Brussett struggled to keep the Cardinals competitive in Week 2.

If the losses start to pile up, the Cardinals will want to get a look at the inexperienced Beck before turning the page to next year's draft class. Journeyman Gardner Minshew is also on the depth chart and is a solid understudy with 47 starts on his resume.

Daniels is set to miss time for the second straight season, so the Washington Commanders will turn to Marcus Mariota again.

Mariota stepped in and threw for 111 yards, one touchdown, and a 109.1 passer rating during Washington's Week 2 loss. He was also mostly steady last season (86.1 QB rating), though he went just 2-6 as the starter. Mariota represents a big step down from Daniels, but he should keep the offense functional for a shorter stretch.

According to NFL Network's Mike Garafolo , the Commanders believe that Daniels' injury won't require surgery and may sideline him for less than a month.

Rookie seventh-round pick Athan Kaliakmanis sits behind Mariota on Washington's depth chart.

Just before the start of the season, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers signed Baker Mayfield to a three-year, $165 million extension. They didn't know at the time that they were paying for the bad version of Baker.

Mayfield has struggled with turnovers and efficiency through the first two weeks. He has completed 71 percent of his passes but has thrown for just 398 yards with a touchdown, an interception, and an 86.6 passer rating. He's also fumbled three times.

It's still early in the year, but Mayfield has looked a lot like the quarterback Cleveland decided to part with after the 2021 season. History suggests that he won't stay down for long, but he's a below-average starter entering Week 3. If he misses time, the Buccaneers could be sunk.

Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels flashed a ton of potential in the preseason, but he obviously has very little NFL experience.

So far, so good for Michael Penix Jr. The third-year quarterback made his 2026 debut on Thursday night and immediately provided a spark to the Atlanta Falcons' offense. In his first action back from a torn ACL, Penix passed for 256 yards, one touchdown, one interception, and a 101.4 QB rating.

If Penix can consistently replicate his Week 3 performance, Atlanta can become a factor in the NFC. However, he was largely average when healthy over his first two seasons.

The Falcons' depth behind him isn't good. Tua Tagovailoa underwhelmed in training camp and the preseason. Although he was set to be the Week 1 starter, an oblique injury sidelined him for the first two weeks. Jack Strand is an unproven undrafted free agent, while Cooper Rush (42.5 QB rating) severely limited Atlanta during its 0-2 start.

Jordan Love took over as the Green Bay Packers' starter in 2023. He played at an above-average level for his first three seasons while leading three consecutive playoff campaigns. However, he has taken a big dip early in 2026.

We can certainly point to Green Bay's shaky offensive line and lack of a consistent run game as the catalysts, but Love hasn't been good enough. He's thrown for 844 yards and six touchdowns, but he's also tossed a pair of interceptions and posted an 83.5 QB rating during the Packers' 1-2 start.

Love hasn't lost the tools and traits needed to be a very good NFL starter, but it's becoming clear that he isn't carry-the-offense good.

If Love is forced to miss time, the Packers can turn to a very experienced backup in Tyrod Taylor, who has a 29-31-1 record as a starter. Kedon Slovis is on Green Bay's practice squad.

Daniel Jones was on his way to being a breakthrough star in 2025 before a torn Achilles ended his season with an 8-5 record. The Giants' 2019 first-round pick hasn't been as sharp this season, though he should improve as he puts more time between himself and the injury.

Jones has only thrown for 376 yards, two touchdowns, two interceptions, and a 79.8 passer rating. However, it's worth noting that he was much better in Week 2 (86.8 QB rating) than in Week 1 (72.8).

The Colts will give Jones plenty of time to progress because he's their clear-cut top option. He received a two-year, $88 million extension this offseason because of that.

2023 first-round pick Anthony Richardson serves as Jones' backup, while 2025 sixth-round pick Riley Leonard is also on the active roster.

Los Angeles Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh didn't do Justin Herbert any favors when he told The White House with Michael Irvin (h/t Michael Davis Smith of ProFootballTalk) that he believes Herbert can be "the best ever to play the position."

However, undue pressure alone doesn't explain Herbert's sudden fall from the upper echelon of quarterbacks. The Oregon product has been an above-average starter since entering the league as a first-round pick in 2020, but he's been well below average so far this season.

Herbert has completed just 59.3 percent of his passes for 401 yards, two touchdowns, three interceptions, and a 71.6 passer rating during Los Angeles' 0-2 start. He has the tools and the traits needed to rebound, but he needs to do it quickly. The Chargers' next six games will be against teams that made the postseason in 2025.

While Herbert hasn't been great, L.A. will be worse off if he goes down. The Chargers have 2025 undrafted free agent DJ Uiagalelei on their practice squad, but Trey Lance is the only other quarterback on the active roster.

The Las Vegas Raiders are in an interesting position. At some point, whether this year or next, they'll turn the reins over to rookie quarterback and No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza . However, the rookie shouldn't start anytime soon.

Kirk Cousins is holding down the fort, as he's proving to be more than just a placeholder. Klint Kubiak would undoubtedly like to see fewer turnovers (three INTs), but Cousins has gone 2-0 while throwing for 413 yards and six touchdowns with a 100.5 passer rating.

It's no longer a stretch to think that Cousins could keep Mendoza on the sideline all season or that the Raiders could make some noise in the playoff mix with him behind center. Las Vegas has a terrific third option providing insurance, too.

Aidan O'Connell has 17 starts on his resume. It wouldn't be a shock to see him draw some trade interest as injuries continue to mount around the league.

The Houston Texans are still waiting on C.J. Stroud to rediscover the Pro Bowl form he had as a rookie in 2023. The Ohio State product has been good enough to put the Texans in the playoffs for three straight years, but he has unquestionably regressed since being named Offensive Rookie of the Year.

Stroud looked a lot like his 2023 incarnation while going throw-for-throw with Josh Allen in Week 1, but he took a big step back in Week. That was likely because of the absence of top receiver Nico Collins.

In all, Stroud has thrown for 627 yards and two touchdowns, posting an 87.5 passer rating this season.

Houston will undoubtedly stick with Stroud for as long as he's healthy. If he is forced to miss time, though, they have a very capable backup in Davis Mills, who went 3-0 last season.

The Minnesota Vikings are firmly in wait-and-see territory at quarterback. Kyler Murray suffered a concussion early in Week 1, so Minnesota still isn't sure what it has in the 2019 first overall pick. However, Murray has been cleared to start in Week 3.

Minnesota knows it has a capable backup in Carson Wentz, who has helped deliver two wins during Murray's absence. Of course, Wentz's numbers haven't been anything special (276 yards, 3 TDs), but he's been smart enough to avoid turnovers while ensuring that he gets Justin Jefferson involved.

If the Vikings were to lose their top two quarterbacks, though, things could get dicey. 2024 first-round pick J.J. McCarthy was once viewed as Minnesota's future. However, he has struggled on the field, struggled to stay healthy, and couldn't even win the backup job this offseason.

It's still too early to know how good the New Orleans Saints can be in 2026. However, quarterback Tyler Shough appears capable of making the sort of second-year jump we saw from Drake Maye in 2025. He nearly led a massive comeback in Week 1. He delivered a comeback victory in Week 2. Along the way, he's tallied some impressive statistics.

Shough has completed 68.9 percent of his passes for 662 yards, four touchdowns, two interceptions, and a 95.7 QB rating. He's also added 31 yards and a touchdown on the ground while fully establishing himself as New Orleans' franchise quarterback.

"I'm such a Tyler Shough guy. Like, he is everything you want from a franchise guy," former Saints tackle Terron Armstead told NFL on CBS .

Backup Spencer Rattler hasn't done much winning with the Saints, but he does have 14 starts on his resume. Third-string quarterback Zach Wilson is a former first-round pick with 33 career starts.

Obviously, the Saints hope that Shough can start every game this season, but they should have enough experience in their QB room to navigate a short-term absence.

Bo Nix produced average-to-above-average statistics during his first two years in the league. However, he played well enough, especially in big moments, to put the Denver Broncos in the playoffs in both 2024 and 2025.

Nix has been more good than great this season. He had a terrible first game back from ankle surgery in Denver's Week 1 loss, but had some late bright moments to bring the Broncos back to win in Week 2.

Overall, Nix has thrown for 419 yards, two touchdowns, two interceptions, and an 83.9 passer rating this season. He'll need to be more consistently efficient for the Broncos to build on their latest win and make another deep playoff push.

If Nix is forced to miss time, Denver can turn to seasoned backup Jarrett Stidham or Sam Ehlinger, who impressed during the preseason.

After being selected first overall in 2021, Trevor Lawrence spent his first few seasons only showing occasional glimpses of being a top-tier NFL quarterback. However, he's shown signs of being special much more consistently since Laim Coen took over as head coach last season.

Lawrence helped lead Jacksonville to an AFC South title last season. He's off to another strong start in 2026. Through two games, Lawrence has passed for 434 yards, four touchdowns, one interception, and a 110.6 QB rating.

The Jaguars should be more than capable of making another postseason push with Lawrence running the offense. However, their playoff hopes likely rest on Lawrence staying healthy. Backup Quinn Ewers went 1-2 as Miami's starter last season. He's the only other quarterback on the active roster.

Nick Mullens and Joey Aguilar are on Jacksonville's practice squad.

After struggling for most of his first two seasons, 2023 first-overall pick Bryce Young has emerged as one of the league's most exciting young signal-callers. So far this season, he's thrown for 648 yards, six touchdowns, and an impressive 113.3 passer rating.

According to Panthers receiver Tetairoa McMillan, the keys to Young's growth aren't difficult to ascertain.

"Just confidence in himself, the play calling and all his playmakers around him," McMillan said, per Joseph Person of The Athletic.

Carolina's backup, Kenny Pickett, has 27 starts on his resume. Undrafted free agent Haynes King is also on the active roster.

Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott might have been a viable MVP candidate last season if not for a historically bad defense. Dallas' defense has yet to show any real improvement in 2026, but Prescott has picked up right where he left off.

Through two weeks, Prescott has completed 73.8 percent of his passes for 454 yards, six touchdowns, an interception, and a 117.1 passer rating. Though he hasn't traditionally been a regular scrambler, Prescott has already rushed for 40 yards as well.

The Cowboys need their defense to improve to make a serious postseason run. They'll also need Prescott to stay healthy. Backup Sam Howell has gone 5-13 as a starter with a 77.5 career QB rating.

Joe Milton III, who is on Dallas' practice squad, has attempted just 53 career passes.

Though he made the Pro Bowl as an alternate as a rookie in 2024, Drake Maye took a dramatic leap in his second season with the New England Patriots. He helped New England reach Super Bowl LX and finished second in MVP voting behind Matthew Stafford.

Maye has shown signs of regression this season, especially when it comes to protecting the football. He's thrown for 386 yards and one touchdown, with four interceptions, 64 rushing yards, and a disappointing 63.1 passer rating.

However, Maye's ceiling is tremendously high. It's reasonable to expect him to return to Pro Bowl form at some point in the not-too-distant future.

While New England's offense won't be as threatening if Maye misses time, the Patriots have a quality backup in Tommy DeVito. He has eight starts and an 88.4 career QB rating on his resume. Rookie seventh-round pick Behren Morton rounds out New England's QB room.

The Detroit Lions haven't looked great during their 1-1 start. That's had a lot to do with their defense and very little to do with the play of quarterback Jared Goff.

Goff, a five-time Pro Bowler, is actually off to one of the best starts of his career. He's thrown for 533 yards, six touchdowns, no interceptions, and a 113.2 QB rating. If he can maintain this level of play, he'll keep Detroit in games more often than not, even with its suspect defense.

Detroit shouldn't worry too much about Goff missing time either, as he's been remarkably durable throughout his career. However, backup Joshua Dobbs has 15 starts under his belt and should be able to fill in for a game or two if needed.

Undrafted rookie Luke Altmyer is on Detroit's practice squad.

Over the last couple of years, the Philadelphia Eagles have earned a reputation as a team that wins with defense and a ground game led by Saquon Barkley. However, Jalen Hurts has repeatedly shown during the postseason that he is one of the league's better quarterbacks.

Hurts is off to a strong start to the 2026 regular season, too. During Philly's 2-0 start, he has thrown for 467 yards, five touchdowns, two interceptions, and a 100.7 QB rating. He has also rushed for 62 yards.

The fact that Hurts has continued to perform well in the wake of the A.J. Brown trade says plenty about his ability to lead the offense. If Hurts cannot lead the team for a game or two due to injury, the Eagles have backup plans.

Andy Dalton is a three-time Pro Bowler with a 70-61-2 career regular-season record who can step in at a moment's notice. Tanner McKee is less experienced but is respected enough that he drew offseason trade interest, according to ESPN's Tim McManus .

Rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton impressed the Eagles enough in the preseason that they kept him on their active roster.

Matthew Stafford is the reigning NFL MVP. After an all-around poor Week 1 performance by the Los Angeles Rams, he has rebounded nicely. Stafford shined in Week 2, despite not having top wideout Puka Nacua in the lineup.

Through two weeks, Stafford has thrown for 482 yards, four touchdowns, two interceptions, and a 101.9 passer rating.

Stafford is still good enough to make a run at MVP while carrying Los Angeles deep into the postseason. The Rams' prospects without him, though, are far less certain.

Backup Stetson Bennett IV saw the first regular-season action of his career in the Rams' 2026 opener, but he has been training for the backup gig for the past two years. Rookie first-round pick Ty Simpson is probably the Rams' future at quarterback, but he may be no more than an emergency option this season.

Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen is probably the early front-runner for league MVP. He won the award two years ago. He's off to a roaring start this season under offensive coordinator-turned-head coach Joe Brady.

Allen has thrown for 582 yards and five touchdowns with a 125.8 passer rating during Buffalo's 2-0 start. He has also rushed for 92 yards and four scores. There simply isn't a quarterback playing better than him through the first two weeks.

Allen's durability over the years should have the Bills confident that he'll carry them through the entire season. He hasn't missed a game due to injury since his rookie season.

If Allen does miss time, though, Buffalo can expect a sizeable drop-off. Kyle Allen is an experienced backup who has made 19 career starts, but he's a pocket passer who cannot mirror Josh Allen's skill set.

Patrick Mahomes is back. While he might not be better than ever, he's shown no negative effects of last year's torn ACL. In fact, he could be in line for one of his best seasons in years.

The 2026 sample size is obviously small, but Mahomes' 103.8 passer rating is his highest since 2022. He was named league MVP that year. He's thrown for 566 yards and five touchdowns with one interception, while rushing for 40 yards and a score.

While another serious injury would derail Kansas City's bid for a comeback campaign, the Chiefs are positioned to survive without Mahomes for a few games if needed.

Justin Fields never developed into a high-end starter, but he's a dynamic dual-threat with 53 starts on his resume. Andy Reid can craft a successful game plan around him. While rookie Garrett Nussmeier is inexperienced, he has all the tools and traits needed to develop into a quality long-term backup.

Lamar Jackson is an MVP-caliber quarterback when he's healthy and at his best. He's been playing well in new coordinator Declan Doyle's offense. Despite dealing with multiple injuries at wide receiver, Jackson has completed 67.9 percent of his passes for 559 yards, two touchdowns, one interception, and a 104.7 passer rating.

Jackson also led the NFL in yards per attempt through the first two weeks, averaging 10 yards per attempt, and has rushed for 74 yards and a score.

While backup Tyler Huntley hasn't had much success outside of Baltimore, he's the perfect backup for the Ravens. His dual-threat playing style meshes perfectly with a playbook tailored to Jackson. He made the Pro Bowl as an alternate with the Ravens in 2022.

Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano rounds out Baltimore's depth chart.

Joe Burrow is widely viewed as a top-five quarterback, even though he hasn't made the playoffs since 2022 and has never won a league MVP award. Of course, Burrow did help carry the Cincinnati Bengals to the Super Bowl in 2021. He's played at an MVP level since then, when healthy, but hasn't had the team success needed to actually win the award.

By his standard, Burrow has been sort of average through the first two weeks. For him, average is 461 passing yards, three touchdowns, one interception, a 96.8 passer rating, and 19 rushing yards.

The lone knock on Burrow has always been his ability to stay healthy. That's why Cincinnati retained Joe Flacco, a former Super Bowl MVP who helped take the Browns to the playoffs just a couple of seasons ago.

Obviously, Flacco is a tier below Burrow, but he posted a 91.0 QB rating with the Bengals last season and could probably start for a few different teams in 2026. Cincinnati also has veteran backup Josh Johnson on its practice squad.

Nothing is guaranteed yet, but it looks like Sam Darnold is ready to return for the Seattle Seahawks. He returned to practice as a full participant on Thursday, aiming to get back on the field for Week 3.

"I'm really striving for that, but I'm just taking it day by day. I don't want to jinx anything," Darnold said, per John Boyle of the team's official website.

Darnold suffered a hip/glute injury early in Week 1 but was tremendous last season while helping to lead Seattle to a Super Bowl XL victory. Backup Drew Lock played extremely well in Darnold's stead this year, posting a league-high 127.3 passer rating and delivering a 2-0 start.

2025 third-round pick Jalen Milroe is also on the depth chart. Of course, it's hard to think he'll see the field behind a QB who has proven he can win a Super Bowl and one who's proven he can keep the offense rolling when called upon.

Brock Purdy is a top-tier quarterback when healthy and playing at his best. He's been in top form for the San Francisco 49ers so far, completing a league-high 80.4 percent of his passes for 492 yards, five touchdowns, one interception, and a 125.6 quarterback rating.

"I don't think he gets enough credit for the way he helps elevate and maximize those around him," one former NFL general manager said of Purdy, per The Athletic's Jeff Howe .

The 49ers also boast one of the league's top backups and the perfect understudy for Kyle Shanahan's offense. Mac Jones started eight games for San Francisco and went 5-3, throwing for 2,151 yards, 13 touchdowns, and six interceptions. Jones was previously a rookie Pro Bowler for the Patriots.

The 49ers know that they can keep the proverbial boat afloat if Purdy misses time in 2026. They also have 2025 seventh-round pick Kurtis Rourke on their active roster.

articles.title: NFL picks: Who the experts predict to win in the Broncos-Rams game
articles.summary: NFL experts make their predictions for the Week 3 clash between the Denver Broncos and Los Angeles Rams.
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos (1-1) and Los Angeles Rams (1-1) have had similar starts to the 2026 season.

Each team was seen as a favorite to reach Super LXI, but each team suffered humbling, one-sided losses to divisional rivals in Week 1. However, each team bounced back in Week 2 with a big victory. Now they meet in a Week 3 prime-time showdown on Sunday Night Football in what many still see as a potential early-season Super Bowl preview.

"They should give the winner of this game a mini Lombardi Trophy since this is the Super Bowl we almost got last season", Breech wrote for CBS. "We came one injury and 6 yards away from getting this game, and honestly, based on how boring Super Bowl LX ended up being, I think I would have preferred this. On paper, I think these two teams are pretty evenly matched, but I think Rams will have two things working against them: They have to play on the road and they have to fly halfway across the country on a short week after playing Monday night.

The NFL scheduling department is clearly trying to break the Rams. After flying 15,842 miles round trip to Melbourne in Week 1, they're now adding 1,724 round-trip miles on this flight to Denver. By the end of Week 3, the Rams will have traveled more miles than 13 different teams will travel ALL SEASON.

That's a lot of jet lag, and as we know, the Rams don't deal well with jet lag. I'll take the Broncos in a thriller."

Gennaro Filice, NFL.com: Rams 23, Broncos 19

"The Super Bowl LX matchup that wasn't!", wrote Filice for NFL.com. "Eight months ago, the Rams and Broncos suffered narrow defeats on Championship Sunday, leaving both painfully short of the Lombardi Trophy game. Then they opened this season by hitting the road and humiliating themselves on national television. Both returned to form at home in Week 2, though, setting up a compelling clash worthy of the Sunday night stage. Showcasing a pair of Super Bowl-winning head coaches and two of the league's most well-rounded rosters, this game doesn't lack for star power. And yet, I see its outcome hinging on the Rams' meat and potatoes, Kyren Williams and Blake Corum . With eerily similar frames, games and jersey numbers (23 and 24), L.A.'s two backs are difficult to tell apart. And so is their robust ground production through two games.

I see Los Angeles ' blue-collar backfield playing a leading role in this prime-time tilt. Denver cleaned up its tackling last week after an embarrassing display against Kansas City 's Kenneth Walker III , but I still think this front's susceptible to the run. Free-agent departure John Franklin-Myers got $63 million for a reason."

"It's a tough road game for the Rams. Denver's pass defense ranks seventh in the NFL, and Bo Nix is 15-3 at home as a starter. With Los Angeles coming off a short week, this is a tough assignment for Matthew Stafford with injuries to Puka Nacua and Myles Garrett , who is out. The Broncos are 5-1-1 ATS as an underdog since last season", wrote Bender for The Sporting News.

"NBC gets a good one for Sunday Night Football in NFL Week 3 with Matthew Stafford vs. Bo Nix and two elite defenses", Cluff wrote for Arizona Republic. "This one might come down to which defense steps up late. It will be the road team."

articles.title: Jayden Maiava is ready to lead USC into battle against Oregon
articles.summary: Ahead of the Trojans’ massive game against Oregon Saturday, a USC Athletics feature looked at Maiava’s unique journey from Hawaii to USC quarterback
articles.body:
On Saturday, USC will host Oregon in a West Coast clash at the Coliseum. Leading the Trojans into battle for the massive game will be redshirt senior quarterback Jayden Maiava.

A recent USC Athletics feature profiled Maiava and his journey from a humble childhood in Hawaii to USC's starting quarterback.

"There nothing average about Trojan quarterback Jayden Maiava or the journey that shaped him," student communications assistant Natalie Miller wrote.

"Bus rides to school at 4 a.m. and practice at the end of the day never fazed him. They were simply part of the journey, another opportunity to prove his commitment by showing up day after day.

"His upbringing came with stretches of poverty and uncertainty, including periods of homelessness and not knowing whether food would be on the table. Those experiences shaped his understanding of what it means to keep going, even when things get difficult.

"This past summer, Maiava showed up for the kids of Hawaii, hosting a free youth football camp in the Palolo Valley that he funded himself. The same community that raised him filled the park, bringing together children and families from all across the island.

"At USC, being the quarterback means more than running the offense. It is a brand in its own rite that carries a unique responsibility and heritage. Through his personal growth, Maiava has defined what that role means to him and established his own place within it."

On Thursday, head coach Lincoln Riley said of Maiava, "He's the guy I want taking us into this game for sure." Against Oregon , USC's quarterback will have the opportunity to deliver his signature moment in Cardinal and Gold to date.

articles.title: Previewing Commanders vs. Seahawks Week 3 matchup
articles.summary: The Commanders have their work cut out for them.
articles.body:
Is it any wonder the Washington Commanders are a big home underdog (+7.5 points) this week?

So often it's not who you play, but when you play them. If the Commanders had played Seattle last week, they would have faced backup quarterback Drew Lock . The Commanders would have started Jayden Daniels . However, it looks like starter Sam Darnold has healed enough to return to his starting role. Commanders backup Marcus Mariota will start for the injured Jayden Daniels Sunday at Northwest Stadium in Landover.

Darnold practiced Thursday and Friday, and he said his goal was to be back on the field this week vs. the Washington Commanders . Darnold missed Week 2 while recovering from being hit from behind when a New England Patriots pass rusher landed on him in the season opener for both teams.

Since 1990, teams that start their NFL season at 0-3 have missed the playoffs that season 97% of the time. The Commanders are currently 0-2 and face the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks (2-0) from last season.

Can you imagine the Seahawks offensive coaches watching film this week of the Commanders' passing defense? The Commanders are the sixth-worst NFL defensive team currently surrendering 6.1 yards per offensive play. The Commanders defense is one of only three teams that hasn't forced a turnover. The Commanders' passing defense has surrendered the most receiving touchdowns thus far, coughing up seven passing touchdowns in only two weeks.

Meanwhile, the Seahawks defense has surrendered the second-lowest point total (17) in the first two weeks, and the second-lowest yards total (428) in the first two games. One must wonder what Marcus Mariota is thinking, getting his chance to play, and he has to face the Seahawks, who are allowing an NFL-best only 3.8 yards per offensive play! They have allowed only 29 first downs, tied for third-best in the NFL.

The Seattle defense has surrendered only 249 passing yards in two games, the best in the NFL. They are the only defense to have intercepted their opposing quarterbacks four times in two weeks.

And then there is Jaxon Smith-Njigba , who leads the NFL through two weeks with 277 receiving yards, 13 receiving first downs and receiving touchdowns (4). Commanders fans can't help but wonder how defensive coordinator Daronte Jones will attempt to defend against JSN.

Chances are very good that Commanders coordinators Daronte Jones and David Blough both had trouble sleeping well this week.

articles.title: Josh Allen: Buffalo Bills quarterback warns NFL rivals of 'special' $2.1bn Highmark Stadium
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills return to new Highmark Stadium on Sunday to face the Los Angeles Chargers with quarterback Josh Allen warning their NFL rivals; Watch Los Angeles Chargers @ Buffalo Bills live on Sky Sports NFL (5.30pm), Sky Sports Main Event (6.30pm) on Sunday
articles.body:
The Bills are perennial Super Bowl contenders and have started this season with wins over Houston and Detroit.

They scored a league-high 77 points through Week 2, with Allen and tight end Dalton Kincaid off to superb starts ahead of their meeting with Los Angeles Chargers - live on Sky Sports NFL from 5.30pm this Sunday .

The Bills opened the stadium's regular-season schedule with a 41-31 victory over the Lion, scoring six touchdowns.

Built next to their old home at a cost of $2.1bn (£1.6bn), superstar Allen threw for three and rushing for two more.

The venue has a natural-grass field with underground heating coils to prevent the surface from freezing, along with what has been described as the world's largest stadium snowmelt system.

"We're here and we are here to stay," Allen told Sky Sports News . "The stadium is awesome. You walk in there and it feels like you're in a different world. It's something I'm proud of to say that I've been first quarterback to play in there, got the first win, and it's a special spot for sure."

In preparation for the Rams, Allen feels it is important to make each match it's own "one-week" season, saying: "Everything we do throughout the week is 'how do we find a way to win' so preparation, having a good practice, trusting teammates, and each week, nothing you did last week carries over to this week.

"Every season is new, every weeks is new, and every game has a different flow. Getting into the game, understanding what the defence is trying to do, what their flavour of the week is, trying to address that and ultimately put more points on the board."

The Bills are among the favourites to represent the AFC Conference in the Super Bowl on Sunday February 14 at SoFi Stadium, the home of the Chargers and Los Angeles Rams in Inglewood, California.

And Allen has compared his upbringing in Firebaugh, California, known being one of the largest irrigated farming communities in the US, to Buffalo, where he moved during the 2018 NFL draft.

"The environment, the family. Everybody feels like they're community here," said Allen. "On Friday nights all the restaurants were closed because everybody was at the game and it's really people looking out for people. To have that special kind of community, I do feel like both my hometown and Buffalo are similar like that.

"I understand the essence of teamwork. I understand that you want to accomplish what you want to accomplish, it takes a village. You have to work hard, you have to want it but there's been so many teammates, friends, family that have helped me get to this spot and I don't take my teammates here for granted, allowing me to go out there and do what I do.

"They work just as hard as I do. To go out on the field and celebrate each others success."

Allen is out to end the long pursuit of a Super Bowl victory for their diehard fans, known as the 'Bills Mafia', with the four-time runners-up from 1991-94 out to finally end the drought.

The 30-year-old added: "There's so many things I'm trying to get better at and trying to perfect my throwing motion but on game day I turn it off and just play football. Hopefully the work that I put up throughout the week and the offseason pays off and I get to go out there and spin the ball how I want to spin it."

articles.title: "You refuse to heal from childhood": Brittany Mahomes speaks out on online hate as Patrick Mahomes defends his wife
articles.summary: Brittany Mahomes has spent years under intense public scrutiny as the wife of Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes.
articles.body: Brittany Mahomes has spent years under intense public scrutiny as the wife of Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes. Her celebrations, social media activity and personal views have repeatedly attracted criticism online. Rather than allowing the noise to dictate how she lives, Brittany has spoken openly about learning to separate strangers’ opinions from her own sense of self. Patrick has also made his position clear when the criticism crossed a line, offering public support for his wife without turning every controversy into a larger spectacle.How Brittany Mahomes responded to years of online criticismThe attention surrounding Brittany increased as Patrick became one of the NFL’s most recognisable stars. Along with praise for the quarterback, she became a frequent target of social media criticism.Brittany has addressed that scrutiny directly. During an Instagram Q&A, she explained how her attitude towards online comments had changed over time.“It used to, yes, but not anymore. I could give two sh*ts about people's opinion of me that don't even know me.”Her response reflected a shift in how she dealt with criticism. Instead of trying to answer every accusation, she appeared more focused on refusing to let strangers define her.Brittany also responded publicly after receiving backlash in 2024 over a Trump-related Instagram like. She wrote:“To be a hater as an adult, you have to have some deep-rooted issues you refuse to heal from childhood. There's no reason your brain is fully developed and you hate to see others doing well.”She later shared a quote about disagreeing without hatred and added, “Read that again!”Another viral episode followed during the AFC Championship, when attention focused on her body language as she walked through a stadium. Brittany responded with another pointed message:“I take rumours as a compliment. The fact that you're bringing my name onto tables I don't sit at shows your obsession. After a video from a Texas Tech basketball game sparked online discussion about Brittany's expressions, Patrick posted:“Man people are weird… love you babe.”Brittany replied, “I love you.”The brief exchange showed Patrick's willingness to stand beside his wife without extending the controversy.Their support has also worked in the opposite direction. articles.title: Travis Kelce’s $200M Garage Beer company steps in to cover Colts star’s $8,847 NFL fine
articles.summary: Travis Kelce’s business ventures have once again found an unexpected way into the NFL conversation.
articles.body: Travis Kelce’s business ventures have once again found an unexpected way into the NFL conversation. Garage Beer, the light beer company backed by Kelce and his brother Jason, reacted after Indianapolis Colts guard Matt Goncalves was fined $8,847 for mimicking a beer chug during a touchdown celebration. Rather than ignore the moment, the brand turned the penalty into a playful marketing opportunity, offering to cover the entire fine. The response quickly caught attention because it matched the company’s casual identity while connecting a football celebration, an NFL rule and one of the league’s most recognisable players.Travis Kelce’s Garage Beer responds to Matt Goncalves’ NFL fineGoncalves landed in trouble after participating in a celebration involving Colts tight end Tyler Warren. Following Warren’s touchdown against the Denver Broncos, he handed the football to Goncalves, who pretended it was a beer can.The guard mimicked opening the top, took an imaginary drink and then spiked the ball. The NFL viewed the gesture differently and classified it as an “offensive demonstration.”Adam Schefter reported the fine on social media, explaining the league’s reasoning. His post included the NFL’s description of the incident:“More: Colts guard Matt Goncalves also was fined $8,847 for engaging Sunday night in what the NFL called an offensive demonstration. ‘Your imitation of chugging a beer constituted an offensive demonstration…in poor taste.’ After Tyler Warren scored, he gave the football to Goncalves, who pretended to pop off its top and celebrate.”Garage Beer quickly joined the conversation with a cheeky response to Schefter’s post.“I think we have another 9K,” the company replied.The comment suggested that Garage Beer was willing to pick up Goncalves’ bill, turning an otherwise routine NFL fine into a piece of brand promotion.Travis Kelce’s $200 million company finds another NFL connectionThe moment also highlighted how closely Garage Beer has become linked with NFL culture. The company, backed by Travis and Jason Kelce, recently completed its first institutional funding round at a reported valuation of around $200 million.For a brand built around a relaxed image and football-friendly humour, the Goncalves incident offered a natural opportunity to engage with fans. The company did not need a traditional advertisement. A few words on social media connected the brand directly to a viral football moment.Goncalves was not the only NFL player fined for a similar celebration. San Francisco 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk reportedly received a $14,926 penalty after mimicking a beer-drinking celebration following a touchdown against Miami. He has reportedly appealed the decision.The NFL's message to both players was clear:“Your imitation of chugging a beer constituted an offensive demonstration and could reasonably be construed as being in poor taste,”Whether Goncalves appeals his fine remains to be seen. articles.body: Simone Biles and Jonathan Owens are making another major move in their home life. The Olympic gymnast and Indianapolis Colts safety have put their Spring, Texas, property on the market for $1.2 million, just days after Biles revealed details of a frightening burglary involving their former Chicago residence.
